newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syrian daily says Netanyahu's survival harms peace.
newsitem.headline: Syrian daily says Netanyahu's survival harms peace.

text.p: An official Syrian newspaper said on Tuesday the Israeli decision not to prosecute Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a corruption scandal undermined hopes for a resumption of Arab-Israeli peace talks.
The English-language daily Syria Times said the decision on Sunday to close the case over Netanyahu's appointment of Roni Bar-On as attorney-general showed that "politics was over law in Israel."

"The Bar-On case points to the real manufacturer of policy in Israel, and how the Israelis deal with peace talks. Everytime the peace talks had reached the point of giving fruits, the military and fanatics turned off the tap," Syria Times said.
"Therefore, and with Israel's will and decision-making concentrated in the hands of the military, no one can expect the American-brokered peace talks to resume and bear fruit," it said.
Syria and Arabs have condemned Netanyahu's refusal to swap occupied Arab land for peace and said his building of Jewish settlements on occupied lands showed he did not want peace.
Syria has held sporadic peace talks with Israel since 1991 but negotiations were stalled over return of the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967.
